summary: A flex block east of Mission Rock Square across Bridgeview Street, on Long Bridge Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, developable as commercial (90 ft) or residential (120 ft) with an elevated sidewalk zone along the boulevard. Unbuilt.

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA and Design Controls that set this block's use and envelope (Resolutions 18-03, 18-04)
Board of Supervisors affirms the EIR certification and approvals (Resolution 33-18); Notice of Determination filed March 9, 2018
Development Agreement and DDA take effect; DA term 30 years, project planned in up to four phases
Draft EIR's illustrative phasing placed Block I in Area 4, 2020-2023; superseded by the DDA phasing
Developer sends the Port its Phase 2 Submittal (with a Garage Report submitted October 14, 2022 and a Basis of Design November 18, 2022); the budget and appraisal elements are deferred
Port Commission finds Phase 2 'not currently financially feasible'; Port and developer agree to decelerate Phase 2 work while monitoring the market (Resolution 23-46)

Port staff say later phases 'may require higher percentages of BMR units' to reach the project's 40% target after Phase 1 was cut to 132 BMR units; the Port, developer and MOHCD are reviewing changes 'to improve the feasibility of future Phases' (Resolution 25-17)

facts.value: Flex block: Commercial Mixed Use or Residential Mixed Use at the developer's choice; maximum height 90 ft if commercial, 120 ft if residential (Figure 6.2)
90 if commercial, 120 if residential; base building 40 ft maximum
If residential: upper building max plan dimension 115 ft, diagonal 150 ft, floorplate 10,000 sq ft; if commercial: floorplate 20,000 sq ft
Long Bridge Street, Terry A. Francois Boulevard (elevated sidewalk zone) and Bridgeview Street facing the square
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 337); future parcel to be ground-leased for 75 years under the DDA
Seawall Lot 337 Associates, LLC (San Francisco Giants and Tishman Speyer), master developer with an option on each vertical parcel
Phase 2 submittal delivered December 2022 but decelerated in 2023 as infeasible; the Port's October 2023 repayment model used a hypothetical Phase 2 start of March 2026

open_questions: Whether Block I will be built residential or commercial has not been decided in any document read.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block I. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel I in Phase 4 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of February 2025 for completing Phase 4's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with the earlier Phase 2 still not begun as of the October 2023 'not currently financially feasible' finding in this record's own milestones. No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 4 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.
